one_liner: Header-only C++17/20 reflection serializer whose struct_pb mode writes protobuf proto3 wire format from plain structs; claims 2.4x/3.4x over protobuf.
what_it_does: iguana serializes ordinary C++ structs to JSON, XML, YAML and the protobuf binary wire format through compile-time reflection. For protobuf you describe the struct with YLT_REFL (field numbers follow member order), YLT_REFL_PB or pb_field helpers (or C++26 [[= iguana::pb_field(N)]] annotations) and call iguana::to_pb(obj, std::string&) / iguana::from_pb(obj, std::string_view); there is no .proto file or protoc step. It is not a drop-in for libprotobuf: there are no generated message classes, descriptors, reflection API, arenas, JSON mapping or text format.
how_it_is_fast: Field layout and wire types are resolved at compile time and inlined, so encode/decode is a straight-line walk over members instead of protobuf's table-driven parser over heap-allocated message objects. Decoding writes into plain std::string/std::vector members (std::string_view members give zero-copy strings), sub-messages are embedded by value rather than heap-allocated, output strings are resized without zero-fill (resize_and_overwrite in C++23, otherwise a private-member access hack on libstdc++/libc++/MSVC STL), and an optional SEQUENTIAL_PARSE fast path matches fields in declaration order before falling back to a field-number map.
when_to_use: You own both C++ endpoints (or must talk proto3 binary to an existing service) and want to keep plain structs instead of protoc-generated classes.
Small-to-medium messages with short strings and few nested messages, decoded into fresh objects without a protobuf Arena, where libprotobuf's per-submessage and per-string heap allocations dominate.
Header-only builds where adding libprotobuf and protoc to the toolchain is unwelcome; also gives JSON/XML/YAML from the same struct definitions.
Already using yalantinglibs (struct_pb there is this library re-exported) or coro_rpc.
when_not_to_use: You need proto2 (required fields, extensions), services, custom options, proto3 JSON mapping or text format; the conformance target covers only the proto3 binary subset.

Schemas are owned as .proto files across languages: field numbers come from C++ member order unless you pin them with YLT_REFL_PB or annotations, so a reordered member silently changes the wire format.

Messages dominated by repeated fixed-width or zigzag integers: issue #301 (2024-09) reported from_pb slower than protobuf ParseFromString on the bench's RepeatIguanaTypeMsg; it was closed with no recorded fix or numbers.
You already decode into protobuf Arenas or reuse message objects: the speedup was never measured against those modes.
You need documented thread safety or a stable ABI: the README FAQ says iguana is not thread-safe yet and tells users to lock around calls.

integration.dependencies: frozen (bundled in the repo); no protobuf runtime for to_pb/from_pb
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (CI: GCC 11.2, Clang 14, AppleClang, MSVC 19.33); C++20 drops the need for YLT_REFL; optional C++26 reflection path needs GCC 16.1 with -std=gnu++26 -freflection
integration.platforms: any platform with those compilers (CI on Linux, macOS, Windows); string resize hack targets libstdc++, libc++ and MSVC STL, other standard libraries fall back to std::string::resize
integration.thread_safety: README FAQ: 'Not yet', lock around calls. from_pb uses function-local static member tables and a thread_local recursion counter.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: wire-compatible with proto3 binary (iguana's bench asserts byte-identical output for most test messages), but the API is free functions on user structs, not protobuf message classes

gotchas: Harness flaw in the reproduction path the claim names: lang/struct_pb_intro.md says to reproduce the 2.4x/3.4x monster numbers with the struct_pack benchmark in alibaba/yalantinglibs. There, src/struct_pack/benchmark/struct_pb_sample.hpp declares Monster(Vec3 a, int32_t b, int32_t c, std::string d, std::string e, Color f, std::vector<Weapon> g, Weapon h, std::vector<Vec3> i) {} with an empty body (present since PR #680 of 2024-05-29, the PR that brought this struct_pb into yalantinglibs, and still at HEAD), so create_monsters() builds struct_pb Monsters with empty name/inventory, no weapons, no path and uninitialized pos/mana/hp/color, while protobuf_sample.hpp fills every field. The MONSTER and MONSTERS rows there time struct_pb on a message holding only a few scalar fields (no strings, weapons or path; protobuf's full monster is about 112 bytes on the wire, derived from the field values) and read indeterminate values. iguana's own benchmark/pb_benchmark.cpp bench3 builds both monsters correctly, so it is unclear which harness produced the published ratios.

iguana's own pb_benchmark.cpp hard-codes '#define SEQUENTIAL_PARSE' (as does yalantinglibs' benchmark.cpp), while the CMake option ENABLE_SEQUENTIAL_PARSE defaults to OFF, so the measured from_pb is a non-default fast path; the input always arrives in declaration order, so it always hits.

The deserialize loops build protobuf messages without an Arena (arena.h is included, data_def.proto sets cc_enable_arenas, but no Arena is used), and all monster strings fit in std::string's small-string buffer, so the gap mostly reflects libprotobuf's roughly a dozen heap allocations per Monster (sub-messages, repeated elements, string objects) against iguana's few vector allocations.

from_pb does not clear the target: parsing into a reused object appends to repeated (std::vector) fields instead of replacing them, unlike ParseFromString. Malformed input throws std::invalid_argument or std::runtime_error, and nesting deeper than 100 throws.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick iguana over hpp-proto when you want protobuf wire compatibility straight from existing C++ structs with no .proto files or codegen step; pick hpp-proto when the schema lives in .proto files, you need proto2, or you want a published Linux comparison against Google protobuf with arenas and stated hardware. Apache Fory C++ and ProtoCache are faster in their own benchmarks but use their own wire formats, not protobuf's.
verified_claims_summary: First-party sentence (lang/struct_pb_intro.md, 2024): in a 'monster' message benchmark, struct_pb serializes 2.4x and deserializes 3.4x faster than Google protobuf's generated C++ code (SerializeToString/ParseFromString). No hardware, compiler, protobuf version or results file is published; the in-repo bench3 is a 100,000-iteration high_resolution_clock loop built at -O3 -g without -DNDEBUG, and the yalantinglibs harness the doc points to times an empty struct_pb Monster against a full protobuf one.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-08-12, C++26 reflection port in May 2026) and Apache-2.0 header-only, so easy to vendor; but the speed claim is first-party, predates the 2026 refactor, and its named reproduction harness benchmarks unequal monster payloads, so treat 2.4x/3.4x as unverified and measure against protobuf with arenas on your own messages.
